row.key_detail: USPSTF grade B (2021) for: Children younger than 5 years

official.topic: Prevention of Dental Caries in Children Younger Than 5 Years: Screening and Interventions
official.recommendation: The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians prescribe oral fluoride supplementation starting at age 6 months for children whose water supply is deficient in fluoride.

row.question_original: Our water supply is low in fluoride. Should our 1-year-old take fluoride supplements?
user_turns: Our water supply is low in fluoride. Should our 1-year-old take fluoride supplements?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies:
The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends that children under the age of 3 years old receive fluoride from their community water supply, formula, or breast milk before considering supplements.

However, if your child's primary source of water is not fluoridated and they are at high risk for tooth decay (e.g., poor oral hygiene, bottle feeding), a pediatrician or dentist may recommend fluoride supplements.

The American Dental Association (ADA) also recommends that children take fluoride supplements only on the advice of their dentist or physician. Before adding any supplements to your child's diet, it's essential to consult with your pediatrician or family dentist to assess the best approach for your child's oral health.

They can help determine if your child is at risk for tooth decay and whether a supplement is necessary.

IT DEPENDS.

Consult with your pediatrician or family dentist to determine if fluoride supplements are necessary for your 1-year-old child, considering the low fluoride levels in your water supply and their individual oral health needs. They can provide personalized advice on whether supplements are required to prevent tooth decay.
